title: Revocation fetch loop has no cap on URLs tried: unbounded validation latency
description:
extract_cdp_http_urls and extract_aia_http_urls return every HTTP/HTTPS URL a certificate advertises, with no limit, and all four fetchers plus both cache wrappers try every one sequentially until one yields a determinative verdict.

Memory is not the concern; latency is. Each attempt carries the transport's own timeout, so total time for one check is (number of URLs) x (timeout). A certificate listing 500 dead CDP URLs against a 10s timeout hangs a single path validation for well over an hour, inside pkix_chain::verify_chain, with no way for the caller to bound it. The accumulated per-URL failure string grows with it and is propagated in RevocationFetchFailed.description.

Exposure is gated behind 'a CA issued this certificate': revocation checking runs after path signature validation, so the extensions are whatever some trusted issuer signed. Public CAs will not issue a cert with hundreds of CDP URLs; a private or unsanitised CA might, and the field is the kind of thing nobody validates. Sibling issue PKIX-rm8.43 files the same class for the AIA certificate-fetch loop (no aggregate byte cap), so the pattern is already recognised in the workspace.

Candidate fix: a documented cap on attempts per check (the loop already stops at the first success, so a cap only bites when URLs are failing), and/or an overall deadline for one revocation check rather than a per-request timeout. The cap value is a policy choice and should be stated, not implicit.

Found while working PKIX-cr8; not one of the ten issues that epic was filed with.
close_reason:
All six check paths now walk at most DEFAULT_MAX_URLS_PER_CHECK (8) URLs, overridable per fetcher with with_max_urls_per_check. URLs are still tried in listed order and the loop still returns on the first determinative verdict, so the cap only bites when URLs are failing and a CA listing its real distribution points first is unaffected.

Eight is grounded, not picked: a census of 773 certificates -- the workspace test corpora including a host trust store (734), plus full chains from twelve major sites across the major commercial CAs (39) -- found a maximum of two HTTP CDP URLs and one HTTP OCSP responder URL, with most carrying one of each. Eight is four times that.

A truncated walk reports both counts via a shared all_urls_failed helper, so the message cannot drift across the six sites and an operator does not read 'all 8 URL(s) failed' for a certificate that listed 500. A cap of 0 attempts nothing and is deliberately not clamped to 1.

What is NOT fixed, and is stated in the constant's documentation rather than left implicit: the cap bounds the number of attempts, not wall-clock latency. A single hung request is the transport's timeout to enforce. An overall per-check deadline would bound the accumulation directly but cannot interrupt an in-flight request, so it complements the cap; not implemented, and it would need a monotonic clock rather than the TimeSource added for PKIX-cr8.6 (a Fixed clock never advances, so a deadline built on TimeSource would silently never trip).

tests/url_cap.rs: 11 tests against a fixture advertising 20 of each kind; 10 fail if the cap is removed, verified. The 11th asserts a check succeeding on its first URL is unaffected, which correctly does not depend on the cap. Commit c6728b3a.
